# Group-aware policy

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-policy` · **Epic:** [#59](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/59) · **Tickets:** 9 (6S 3M)

Allow entries and MCP tool `allowWhen` conditions can be limited to IdP groups or specific users with `groups: [...]` / `users: [...]`. Entries without these fields behave exactly as today. A scoped entry never allows a request without a valid verified identity, a non-member is denied outright and never sent to the judge, and workers on older releases deny scoped destinations instead of allowing them. `warden policy eval` replay shows which users a candidate change affects.

## How we build it

- Schema: `config.AllowlistEntry` gains `Groups []string` and `Users []string` (yaml/json omitempty), and `config.MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition` gain `Groups`/`Users` next to `AgentID`/`TimeWindow`. Validation trims, rejects empty values, deduplicates and sorts, and caps each list at 256 values of 256 bytes. A Users value containing '@' is an email and is lowercased; any other value is an exact `sub`. Groups are exact, case-sensitive literals. The denylist and task-scope (`mcp.scopes.list[].constraints`) allowWhen get no scoping in P1. Entries without the fields marshal byte-identically to today, so existing ETags do not change. Old binaries reading a new local YAML fail at startup (KnownFields(true)), which fails closed.
- Merge safety: until enforcement lands, validation rejects non-empty Groups/Users with `not yet enforced`. W-P1-GPOL-03 lifts the guard for allow entries and W-P1-GPOL-04 for MCP tool conditions, and both depend on the fail-closed wire (W-P1-GPOL-06), so main never parses a scoped rule that some worker would treat as global.
- Fail-closed wire: the CP keeps serving one shared, ETag-versioned body. When building `policyWire` it moves allow entries that have groups/users out of `allowlist` into a new `scopedAllowlist` field, and for MCP tools with a scoped allowWhen it puts the real condition in a new wire-only `AllowWhenScoped` field and sets the legacy `AllowWhen` to a reserved AgentID sentinel `!identity-scoped` (rejected by validation as a real agent id). New workers merge both back in `parseRemotePolicy`. Old workers ignore the unknown fields, so scoped destinations stay NoMatch (denied) and scoped tools fail the sentinel condition (denied). The worker heartbeat adds `features: ["groupPolicy"]` for visibility only, and the fleet view flags workers without it while scoped rules exist.
- Subject: one type, `identity.Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}`, defined with `SubjectFrom` and `Claims.EmailVerified` in the leaf package `internal/identity` by W-P1-VRFY-01, used by internal/policy, internal/mcp/gateway and internal/policyeval. `identity.SubjectFrom(claims, status)` returns nil unless the identity status is valid, so missing, invalid and expired tokens give a nil subject. A `users` email entry matches only when EmailVerified is true; `sub` entries always match exactly. P2 worker-bound and P3 per-user-limits extend this type rather than redefine it.
- Evaluator: `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result{Decision, Reason, Scoped}`; `Evaluate` keeps its signature and only ever returns Allow, Deny or NoMatch (a scoped-only match with no subject collapses to Deny). `load()` precompiles per-entry group/user sets and a `hasScoped` flag, so policies without scoped entries keep the current zero-alloc path. Per entry the order is port and domain, then principal, then time window, then rate limit, so non-members never consume a scoped entry's budget. A destination matched only by scoped entries returns `Conditional` (reason `identity_required`) for a nil subject and `Deny` (reason `group_not_allowed`) for a non-member; neither is judge-eligible. The denylist is still checked first. Rate-limit counters for scoped entries are keyed per entry index (today the key is `domain:port`, shared across entries); unscoped keys are unchanged. Per-user limits come in P3.
- CONNECT path: `handleConn` switches exhaustively on the decision, with default meaning deny. Conditional without a CA gives 403 `identity_required`. Conditional with a CA proceeds to TLS with a `deferred` enum {none, judge, identity} that replaces the `needsJudge bool` passed to `handleTLS`; every non-HTTP/1 branch there (non-TLS bytes, h2 ALPN or preface/gRPC, unknown protocol inside TLS) fails closed when deferred != none. An Allow granted by a scoped entry using the Proxy-Authorization subject is allowed; without a CA the raw tunnel is closed at the token's `exp`. h2/gRPC clients must send identity on CONNECT.
- Request path: a new `scopedPolicyStage` runs after `identityStage` (and the user block check) and before `judgeGate`, on every request of any session whose CONNECT result was Scoped or Conditional, calling the live evaluator with that request's subject. Keep-alive requests from different users and mid-session policy swaps are each decided correctly. In these sessions scoped rate limits are charged per request, and the CONNECT-time check uses a non-charging `PeekFor` (new). Deny writes 403 with Event.Reason and the decision-log reason `identity_required` or `group_not_allowed` plus the VRFY user fields.
- MCP: `OnRequest` gains a `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject *identity.Subject}` parameter on proxy.MCPGateway, proxy.WSScanner and the ws.Pump interface, and on all callers and fakes. http.go passes the request subject; ws.Pump stores the subject verified on the upgrade request; the stdio pump passes nil, so group-gated tools are denied over stdio. `compileConditions` adds group/user sets and `conditionDenies` fails with the existing Kind `mcp_tool_condition` and Detail `no verified identity` or `user not permitted`. P1 gates whole tools only; per-group argument constraints come later. The session key (`agentID:domain`) is unchanged in P1.
- Replay and lint: `policyeval.Evaluate` builds a subject from Event.UserSub/UserEmail/UserGroups only when the recorded identity status is valid, and maps Conditional to deny. EvalDiff gains `AffectedUsers` (up to 20, sorted), `AffectedUsersTotal` and `AnonymousCount`. `warden policy eval` prints them and accepts `--user`. A new `config.LintScoped` warns about scoped entries shadowed by an unscoped or wildcard entry for the same destination; workers log once per agent when scoped entries exist but that agent's identity mode is off.
- Observability: `RecordBlocked("identity_required"|"group_not_allowed")` and a new OTel counter `warden.policy.scoped.total{result=allow|not_member|no_identity}` (Prometheus name warden_policy_scoped_total) with no user or group labels. Raw tokens, group lists and emails never appear in metric labels or debug logs.
- Dashboard: the CP policy editor adds groups/users chip inputs per allow entry and per MCP allowWhen, saved through `/dashboard/api/policy` and the existing policyYAML write path; the worker and CP policy views show a `scoped` badge and the lint warnings. Sorted, normalized groups/users keep ETags and the P1 policy-history diff deterministic.

## Done when

On a CA-enabled worker in attribute mode with `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` and no unscoped entry for that host: a valid Dex token for an eng member is allowed over both Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity; a non-member gets 403 `group_not_allowed`; anonymous, invalid and expired tokens get 403 `identity_required`; within one keep-alive session requests from different users are each decided correctly; a Conditional CONNECT with no CA, or one that switches to h2 or raw bytes, is denied and the judge is never consulted. An MCP tool with `allowWhen.groups: [finance]` is denied to eng and allowed to finance in enforce mode. A worker on the previous release that receives this policy from the CP denies api.github.com and the gated tool, and the fleet view flags it. `warden policy eval` against a candidate that removes eng access lists only the affected eng users plus a count of anonymous events. Deny events, decision logs and metrics carry the two new reasons.

### 1/9 · W-P1-GPOL-01

**Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#60](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/60)

Add `Groups`/`Users` to `config.AllowlistEntry` and `config.MCPToolCondition` with normalization, deep copies and a fail-closed validation guard. Until the evaluator and gateway enforce these fields, any config that sets them is rejected, so main never parses a scoped rule that would be treated as global. This ticket is config-only; the old-worker wire handling is W-P1-GPOL-06.

**Requirements**

- `AllowlistEntry` gains `Groups []string` and `Users []string` (yaml `groups`/`users`, json `groups,omitempty`/`users,omitempty`); `MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition` gain the same, populated in the raw-to-typed conversion in mcp.go.
- Normalization: trim each value, reject empty strings, deduplicate and sort, cap each list at 256 values of at most 256 bytes. A Users value containing '@' is lowercased as an email; any other value is an exact sub. Groups stay case-sensitive.
- Guard: `Validate` and `validateMCPConstraints` reject any non-empty Groups/Users with an error naming the field path and `not yet enforced`. GPOL-03 and GPOL-04 lift it per path.
- Scoped fields stay rejected permanently in P1 on denylist entries (strict KnownFields) and in task-scope `mcp.scopes.list[].constraints` allowWhen.
- The AgentID value `!identity-scoped` is reserved and rejected in any allowWhen.
- `Policy.DeepCopy`, the constraint clone helper in mcp.go and `copyToolConstraints` in settings.go clone the Groups/Users slices.
- Entries without the fields marshal byte-identically to today in YAML and JSON.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/config.go: add the fields to `AllowlistEntry`; deep-copy them in `Policy.DeepCopy`.
2. internal/config/mcp.go: add the fields to `MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition`; copy them in the raw conversion and the AllowWhen clone helper.
3. internal/config/settings.go: deep-copy Groups/Users in `copyToolConstraints`.
4. internal/config: new `normalizePrincipals(path string, groups, users []string) ([]string, []string, error)` called from `Validate` and `validateMCPConstraints`, followed by the temporary guard error.
5. configs/config.example.yaml: add commented examples under policy.allowlist and an mcp.tools.constraints allowWhen.
6. Tests in internal/config: normalization table, guard rejection, reserved sentinel, JSON/YAML round-trip of normalized values (via the unexported normalizer), and aliasing tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `groups: [' eng ', eng]` and `users: [Alice@Corp.Example, 'u-123']`, the normalizer returns Groups==[eng] and Users==[alice@corp.example, u-123]: `go test ./internal/config -run TestNormalizePrincipals`.
- [ ] Given any allow entry or MCP allowWhen with non-empty groups, loading the config fails with an error naming the field path.
- [ ] Given `groups` on a denylist entry or in a task-scope allowWhen, loading fails.
- [ ] Given a DeepCopy of a policy with Groups, mutating the copy's Groups[0] leaves the original unchanged: `go test ./internal/config -run TestDeepCopy_GroupsNotAliased`.
- [ ] Existing config tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/config`.

### 2/9 · W-P1-GPOL-02

**Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#61](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/61)

Add `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result` to `internal/policy` so allow entries can be limited to groups and users. A non-member must get an explicit Deny that never reaches the judge, a missing identity must give `Conditional`, and non-members must not consume a scoped entry's rate budget. `Evaluate` keeps returning only Allow, Deny or NoMatch, so existing callers cannot treat the new value as an allow.

**Requirements**

- Use `identity.Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}` and `SubjectFrom(claims, status)` from internal/identity, defined by W-P1-VRFY-01; never define a second Subject in internal/policy.
- `Result{Decision, Reason string, Scoped bool}`; new Decision `Conditional` whose String() is `conditional`. `Evaluate(d, p, s)` returns EvaluateFor(..., nil).Decision with Conditional mapped to Deny.
- Per entry: port and domain, then principal (sub match, verified-email match, or any shared group), then time window, then rate limit. Unscoped entries match everyone.
- Destination matched only by scoped entries: nil subject gives Conditional with reason `identity_required`; non-nil non-member gives Deny with reason `group_not_allowed`. Neither ever returns NoMatch. The denylist still wins.
- Rate-limit counters for scoped entries are keyed by entry index plus domain:port; unscoped keys stay `domain:port`. New `PeekFor` evaluates without charging counters.
- `load()` precompiles group/user sets and `hasScoped` under swapMu; with no scoped entries EvaluateFor(nil) takes the current path with zero extra allocations.
- `handleConn` in internal/proxy/serve.go switches exhaustively on Decision with default meaning deny, so any future value fails closed.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/identity (from W-P1-VRFY-01): use `Subject`, `SubjectFrom` and Claims.EmailVerified as defined there.
2. internal/policy/policy.go: add `Conditional`, `Result`, per-entry `principals` sets and `hasScoped` in `load()`.
3. internal/policy/policy.go: refactor the body of `Evaluate` into a new `evaluate(domain, port, scheme, subj, charge bool) Result`; add `EvaluateFor` and `PeekFor` wrappers; key scoped rate limits by index.
4. internal/proxy/serve.go `handleConn`: replace the `== Deny`/`== NoMatch` checks with an exhaustive switch (default deny); behaviour for existing decisions is unchanged.
5. internal/policy/policy_test.go: table tests for member, non-member, nil subject, unverified email, mixed scoped/unscoped, deny-wins, shared-domain rate buckets and non-members not consuming budget.
6. Add `BenchmarkEvaluate` (50 unscoped entries) and `BenchmarkEvaluateForScoped` (50 scoped entries, 100-group subject) in internal/policy.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}`, EvaluateFor gives Allow for [eng], Deny/`group_not_allowed` for [sales] and Conditional/`identity_required` for nil, and Evaluate gives Deny: `go test ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_Scoped`.
- [ ] Given `users: [alice@corp.example]`, a subject with that email and EmailVerified=false gets Deny; with EmailVerified=true it gets Allow.
- [ ] Given a scoped entry with rateLimit 1/minute, non-member and nil-subject calls followed by a member call still give Allow for the member.
- [ ] Existing tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/policy ./internal/proxy`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/policy -run '^$' -bench 'BenchmarkEvaluate' -count 10` compared with benchstat against main shows 5% or less ns/op change and 0 extra allocs/op for BenchmarkEvaluate.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/policy -run TestEvaluateFor_ConcurrentReplace` passes.

### 3/9 · W-P1-GPOL-03

**Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#62](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/62)

Enforce scoped allow entries in the worker at CONNECT and on every request, then lift the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard for allow entries. One keep-alive session can carry requests from different users, so the decision must be re-made per request with that request's subject. Every path that cannot see the request (no CA, raw TLS, h2/gRPC, non-TLS bytes) fails closed, and the judge is never consulted for a scoped destination.

**Requirements**

- handleConn calls EvaluateFor with the CONNECT subject from W-P1-VRFY-02, non-nil only when the Proxy-Authorization token is valid and the agent's identity mode is attribute.
- Conditional without a CA: 403 `identity_required`. Conditional with a CA: proceed to TLS with `deferred=identity`; `handleTLS` takes a new `deferred` enum {none, judge, identity} instead of `needsJudge bool`, and every non-HTTP/1 branch fails closed when deferred != none.
- A scoped Allow at CONNECT without a CA becomes a raw tunnel that is closed at the token's exp.
- New `scopedPolicyStage` after identityStage and the user block check, before judgeGate, runs on every request of a Scoped or Conditional session against the live evaluator. Deny or Conditional gives 403 with reason `group_not_allowed` or `identity_required`.
- Deny events, decision logs and `RecordBlocked` carry the new reasons plus the VRFY user fields; new OTel counter `warden.policy.scoped.total{result}`. `identity_required` and `group_not_allowed` are added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06) and, when docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json exists, to its reason enum with a schema_rev bump. Raw tokens are never logged.
- When scoped entries exist and an agent's identity mode is off, log one warning per agent with the count of scoped entries.
- With no scoped entries, CONNECT and request behaviour, events and metrics are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/proxy/serve.go `handleConn`: call `PeekFor` with the CONNECT subject; handle Conditional and Scoped results in the exhaustive switch; wrap the raw tunnel in an exp deadline for scoped Allow.
2. internal/proxy/tls.go `handleTLS`: replace `needsJudge bool` with a new `deferred` type and fail closed on non-TLS, h2/gRPC and unknown-protocol branches when deferred != none.
3. internal/proxy/http.go: add `scoped bool` to requestScope and a new `scopedPolicyStage` in the stage list after identityStage; it calls `EvaluateFor` and short-circuits judgeGate.
4. internal/proxy metrics seam: add the scoped counter (new method) and record the two reasons.
5. internal/config: remove the allow-entry part of the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard.
6. Tests in internal/proxy with the VRFY fake verifier and a fake judge covering every acceptance case.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` and a CA, an eng token on Proxy-Authorization is forwarded and a sales token gets 403 `group_not_allowed`: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_ConnectIdentity`.
- [ ] On one keep-alive tunnel with no Proxy-Authorization, an eng X-Warden-Identity request gets 200 and a following sales request gets 403: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestGroupPolicy_RequestIdentity`.
- [ ] Without a CA, an anonymous CONNECT to a scoped-only host gets 403 with a deny event reason `identity_required`.
- [ ] With a CA and a Conditional CONNECT, sending non-TLS bytes or negotiating h2 closes the connection with no upstream dial and a deny event.
- [ ] With a judge fake that always allows, non-member and anonymous requests to a scoped-only host are denied and the fake gets zero calls.
- [ ] An expired token on a request to a scoped-only host is denied with identity_status=expired on the event.

### 4/9 · W-P1-GPOL-04

**Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#63](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/63)

Let `allowWhen` on an MCP tool require a group or user, so a tool the policy allows can be limited to, for example, finance. The gateway needs the request subject, so the `OnRequest` seam gains a `RequestMeta` parameter on every interface and caller. A failure uses the existing Kind `mcp_tool_condition`; a nil subject never satisfies a group or user condition.

**Requirements**

- New `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject *identity.Subject}` parameter on OnRequest in proxy.MCPGateway, proxy.WSScanner, the ws.Pump interface, the gateway and all fakes.
- http.go `mcpRequestScan` passes the request's verified subject; ws.Pump stores the subject verified on the upgrade request; the stdio pump passes nil (documented: group-gated tools are denied over stdio).
- `compiledCondition` gains group/user sets; `conditionDenies` fails when the condition has groups/users and the subject is nil or not a member, using one shared membership helper in internal/identity.
- Failure emits Kind `mcp_tool_condition` with Detail `no verified identity` or `user not permitted`; enforce mode blocks, monitor mode records and passes. Group names never appear in Detail or metric labels.
- Conditions only narrow: a tool denied by allow/deny or scope is never re-permitted.
- Remove the MCP tool-level part of the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard; task-scope allowWhen stays rejected for groups/users.
- The session key (`agentID:domain`) is unchanged; per-user call-chain state is a known limitation.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcp/gateway: add `RequestMeta`; change `OnRequest` to take it and pass the subject to `conditionDenies`.
2. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go `compileConditions`: build group/user sets from `AllowWhen.Groups/Users`.
3. internal/proxy/proxy.go and internal/mcp/ws/pump.go: update the three interface declarations; ws.Pump gets a `Subject` field set by the proxy at upgrade.
4. internal/proxy/http.go `mcpRequestScan` and internal/mcp/stdio/pump.go: pass the subject or nil.
5. Update fakes in mcp_seam_test.go and ws_seam_test.go; add gateway tests and a proxy seam test that the subject reaches the gateway.
6. internal/config: lift the MCP tool allowWhen guard.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given tools.allow [pay] and constraints.pay.allowWhen{groups:[finance]} in enforce mode, an eng subject is denied with Kind mcp_tool_condition and a finance subject passes: `go test ./internal/mcp/gateway -run TestConditionGroups`.
- [ ] A nil subject (stdio or anonymous) is denied with Detail `no verified identity`.
- [ ] In monitor mode an eng call passes and the finding is recorded.
- [ ] Over WebSocket, the subject from the upgrade request is used for each frame: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestMCPWS_SubjectFromUpgrade`.
- [ ] Existing suites pass with the new signature: `go test ./internal/mcp/... ./internal/proxy`.

### 5/9 · W-P1-GPOL-05

**Show affected users in policy eval replay**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#64](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/64)

Make `policyeval.Evaluate` replay events with the recorded user so `warden policy eval` shows which users a candidate change affects. Events without a valid recorded identity replay as anonymous and are counted separately, so pre-identity traffic is not mistaken for user impact. Also add `config.LintScoped` and print its warnings. The dashboard editor moved to W-P1-GPOL-08.

**Requirements**

- Build the subject from Event.UserSub/UserEmail/UserGroups only when the recorded identity status is valid; otherwise nil. Conditional and NoMatch replay as deny.
- EvalDiff gains `AffectedUsers []string` (distinct, email else sub, sorted, capped at 20), `AffectedUsersTotal int` and `AnonymousCount int`; the diff key (domain, port, method) is unchanged.
- `warden policy eval` prints affected users under each regression line and accepts `--user` to filter events to one sub or email.
- Replay keeps groups/users on the replay policy; rateLimit and timeWindow are still stripped as today.
- New `config.LintScoped(p Policy) []string` warns about scoped entries shadowed by an unscoped or wildcard entry for the same destination; `warden policy eval` prints the warnings.
- Output contains only sub/email, never tokens or full group lists. Recorded groups are a point-in-time snapshot (documented in the command help).

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/policyeval/eval.go: build the subject per event, call `EvaluateFor`, map Conditional to deny.
2. internal/policyeval/eval.go: track a per-diff user set and anonymous count; add the new EvalDiff fields.
3. internal/config: new `LintScoped` with table tests.
4. cmd/proxy/eval.go: print affected users and lint warnings; add the `--user` flag.
5. Tests in internal/policyeval and cmd/proxy.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given alice (groups [eng], valid) and bob (groups [sales], valid) both allowed to api.github.com, a candidate scoping it to [sales] gives one NewDenies entry with AffectedUsers==[alice]: `go test ./internal/policyeval -run TestEvaluate_AffectedUsers`.
- [ ] An event with identity status expired replayed against a scoped-only candidate counts in AnonymousCount.
- [ ] With 25 distinct affected users, AffectedUsers has 20 entries and AffectedUsersTotal is 25.
- [ ] A scoped entry for api.github.com plus an unscoped `*.github.com` entry produces a shadow warning: `go test ./internal/config -run TestLintScoped`.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestEvalCmd_AffectedUsers` shows the affected-users line.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-02`](identity-policy.md#29--w-p1-gpol-02) Make the policy evaluator subject-aware with EvaluateFor; [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#37--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync

### 6/9 · W-P1-GPOL-06

**Project scoped rules into fail-closed policy wire fields**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Old workers decode the CP policy with lenient JSON, so they would drop `groups` and treat a scoped entry as global. The CP keeps one shared ETag body but moves scoped allow entries into a new `scopedAllowlist` field and replaces scoped MCP allowWhen with a reserved sentinel, so old workers deny and new workers merge the real rules back. This must land before GPOL-03/04 lift the validation guard.

**Requirements**

- `policyWire` gains `ScopedAllowlist []config.AllowlistEntry json:"scopedAllowlist,omitempty"`; allow entries with groups/users are moved there and left out of `allowlist`.
- For tools whose allowWhen has groups/users, the wire carries the real condition in a new wire-only `AllowWhenScoped` field (`yaml:"-"`) and sets `AllowWhen` to `{AgentID: "!identity-scoped"}`.
- `parseRemotePolicy` and the SettingsWire apply step merge `scopedAllowlist` and `AllowWhenScoped` back (keeping entry order deterministic) and fail the pull if a sentinel remains without a scoped condition.
- Policies without scoped rules produce byte-identical wire JSON and the same ETag as before.
- Serving stays one body per ETag; no per-worker policy bodies.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `ScopedAllowlist` to `policyWire` and a new `projectScoped(p config.Policy, s *config.SettingsWire)` used where the wire is built in policyserver.go.
2. internal/config/mcp.go: add the wire-only `AllowWhenScoped` field to `MCPToolConstraints` and copy it in the clone helpers.
3. internal/config/remote.go: extend `remoteWire` with `ScopedAllowlist` and merge it in `parseRemotePolicy`; restore AllowWhen from AllowWhenScoped.
4. Tests: golden wire for an unscoped policy; projection test; an old-worker simulation that decodes with the pre-change struct and gets NoMatch and a sentinel-denied tool.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An unscoped policy serves the same body and ETag as the pre-change golden: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPolicyWire_UnscopedUnchanged`.
- [ ] A scoped entry is absent from `allowlist` and present in `scopedAllowlist`, and a new worker's parsed Policy contains it with Groups set: `go test ./internal/config -run TestParseRemotePolicy_Scoped`.
- [ ] Decoding the wire with the previous `remoteWire` shape yields no allow entry for the scoped host and an allowWhen that the current gateway denies.
- [ ] A pull whose settings contain the sentinel without AllowWhenScoped fails with an error and the worker keeps its last good policy.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-01`](identity-policy.md#19--w-p1-gpol-01) Add groups/users to allow entries and MCP conditions schema

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-GPOL-03`](identity-policy.md#39--w-p1-gpol-03) Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time; [`W-P1-GPOL-04`](identity-policy.md#49--w-p1-gpol-04) Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions; [`W-P1-GPOL-07`](identity-policy.md#79--w-p1-gpol-07) Report groupPolicy support in heartbeat and flag old workers

### 7/9 · W-P1-GPOL-07

**Report groupPolicy support in heartbeat and flag old workers**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Operators need to see which workers do not understand scoped rules, because those workers deny scoped destinations. Workers add `features: ["groupPolicy"]` to the heartbeat body, and the fleet view flags workers without it while the served policy has scoped rules. This is visibility only; the wire fail-closed behaviour is W-P1-GPOL-06.

**Requirements**

- `RemoteProvider.Heartbeat` sends `features` next to `policyETag`; the body stays under the CP's 4096-byte limit.
- `handleHeartbeat` decodes `features` (bounded to 16 entries of 64 bytes) and `WorkerRegistry` stores them.
- The fleet view shows a `no groupPolicy` badge for workers lacking it when the current policy has scoped rules.
- The CP logs once per worker per ETag with proxy_id and scoped_entries count, never group names.
- Heartbeats without `features` keep working.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/remote.go `Heartbeat`: add the features field.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go `handleHeartbeat` and seams.go: pass features into a new registry method.
3. internal/controlplane/registry.go: store features per worker and expose them in the fleet snapshot.
4. internal/dashboard: render the badge in the fleet view.
5. Tests in internal/controlplane and internal/config.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A heartbeat with `{"policyETag":"x","features":["groupPolicy"]}` stores the feature: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestHeartbeat_Features`.
- [ ] A legacy heartbeat `{"policyETag":"x"}` is still accepted and the worker is flagged when scoped rules exist.
- [ ] A heartbeat with 100 features stores at most 16.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-06`](identity-policy.md#69--w-p1-gpol-06) Project scoped rules into fail-closed policy wire fields

### 8/9 · W-P1-GPOL-08

**Edit groups/users in the dashboard policy editor**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

Let admins add groups/users to allow entries and MCP allowWhen in the CP policy editor, and show which rules are scoped. The editor saves through the existing `/dashboard/api/policy` write path and `config.AllowlistEntry`, so validation and normalization come from the config loader. Lint warnings from `config.LintScoped` are shown next to the entries.

**Requirements**

- Chip inputs for groups and users per allow entry and per MCP tool allowWhen; values are escaped before rendering.
- Saves use the existing editor method on `/dashboard/api/policy`; the CP validates through the same config loader and returns 400 with the error on invalid input, leaving the served policy unchanged.
- Worker and CP policy views show a `scoped` badge; the worker dashboard stays read-only.
- Lint warnings from `config.LintScoped` are returned by the GET and shown in the editor.
- Saved groups/users come back normalized and sorted so ETags and history diffs are stable.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/dashboard/index.html: add chip inputs and the scoped badge in the policy list and MCP editor.
2. internal/dashboard policy handlers: include `lint` in the GET response.
3. internal/controlplane write path: confirm groups/users round-trip through policyYAML.
4. Tests in internal/dashboard and internal/controlplane for round-trip and validation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Saving `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng], users: [Alice@Corp.Example]}` returns and re-reads groups [eng] and users [alice@corp.example]: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestPolicyEdit_ScopedRoundTrip`.
- [ ] Saving an empty group value returns 400 and the served ETag is unchanged.
- [ ] A chip value containing `<script>` renders as text (escaping test in the dashboard JS test or a Go template test).

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-GPOL-03`](identity-policy.md#39--w-p1-gpol-03) Apply group-aware allow decisions at CONNECT and request time; [`W-P1-GPOL-04`](identity-policy.md#49--w-p1-gpol-04) Support groups/users in MCP tool allowWhen conditions; [`W-P1-GPOL-05`](identity-policy.md#59--w-p1-gpol-05) Show affected users in policy eval replay
